newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian metalworkers wage talks break down.
newsitem.headline: Italian metalworkers wage talks break down.

text.p: Negotations between trades unions and employers over the renewal of contracts for some 1.5 million engineer and metalworkers have broken down, union sources said on Thursday.
Earlier this week, unions called an eight-hour strike on September 27 in support of their pay claim. No new date for a fresh round of talks between the two sides has been set.
"The differences between the two sides are greater than ever," a union source close to the negotiations said.

Metalworkers' unions representing staff at key Italian industrial companies such as carmaker Fiat and information technology group Olivetti have demanded an overall wage rise of 10.1 percent over the next two years.
Employers' group Federmeccanica has offered unions a range of increases of between seven and nine percent -- in line with contracts already renewed in various other Italian sectors.
Talks between unions and Federmeccanica resumed again on Thursday after being suspended in July.
Italy's centre-left government has not interevened in the dispute but has urged moderate wage increases as it battles to keep inflation on a downward path. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
